'''Kanasa Mori-sumi''' (金刺 盛澄, also known as Suwa Mori-sumi) was a priest ({{ill|Hōri|ja|大祝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōhō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祝 (神職)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24869239}}) and samurai of the {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}} Lower Shrine during the late {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}.<ref>[https://suwacitymuseum.jp/nandemo/koumoku/1000/100115.htm  諏訪市博物館 - ''Suwa City Museum: Kanasa Mori-sumi'']</ref> He is also referred to as {{ill|Kana Moritomo|ja|諏訪盛澄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Mori-sumi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金刺盛澄|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11646497}}.<ref>[https://suwacitymuseum.jp/nandemo/gojuuon/13_su/~su_69.htm  ''Suwa City Museum: Suwa Mori-sumi'']</ref> His younger brother was {{ill|Tezuka Mitsumori|ja|手塚光盛}}.

## Biography
Initially, Kanasa Mori-sumi joined {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|en|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|qid=Q1139202|lt=Minamoto no Yoshinaka}} during the {{ill|Genpei War|en|Genpei War|qid=Q737542|lt=Genpei War}} but later returned to his homeland to oversee the {{ill|Misayama Ritual|ja|御射山神事}} and left his younger brother Mitsumori in his stead. Due to his longstanding affiliation with the {{ill|Ise Heishi|ja|平家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heike|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢平氏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q15734686}}, recorded in the ''{{ill|Azuma Kagami|en|Azuma Kagami|qid=Q1042324|lt=Azuma Kagami}}'' under the entry for {{ill|Bunji (era)|en|Bunji (era)|qid=Q1194415|lt=Bunji}} 3 (1187), August 15, Mori-sumi was captured by {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ar|ميناموتو نو يوريتومو|be|Мінамота-но Ёрытома|bg|Минамото но Йоритомо|br|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ca|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ckb|مینامۆتۆ نۆ یۆریتۆمۆ|cs|Joritomo Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoritomo|el|Μιναμότο νο Γιοριτόμο|eo|Minamoto no Yoritomo|es|Minamoto no Yoritomo|eu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fa|میناموتو نو یوریتومو|fi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|fr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|hak|Minamoto no Yoritomo|he|מינאמוטו נו יוריטומו|hu|Minamoto no Joritomo|id|Minamoto no Yoritomo|it|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝|ko|미나모토노 요리토모|la|Minamoto no Yoritomo|lt|Minamoto no Joritomo|mr|मिनामोटो नो योरिमोटो|ms|Minamoto no Yoritomo|nl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|pl|Yoritomo Minamoto|pt|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ro|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ru|Минамото-но Ёритомо|sh|Minamoto no Yoritomo|sk|Joritomo Minamoto|sl|Minamoto no Joritomo|sq|Minamoto no Joritomo|sr|Минамото но Јоритомо|sv|Minamoto no Yoritomo|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยริโตโมะ|tl|Minamoto no Yoritomo|tr|Minamoto no Yoritomo|uk|Мінамото-но Йорітомо|vi|Minamoto no Yoritomo|war|Minamoto no Yoritomo|wuu|源赖朝|zh|源赖朝|zh_min_nan|Minamoto no Yoritomo|zh_yue|源賴朝|zu|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}} and placed under the custody of {{ill|Kajiwara Kagetoki|en|Kajiwara Kagetoki|qid=Q3191855|lt=Kajiwara Kagetoki}}.

Yoritomo initially intended to execute Mori-sumi. However, Kagetoki, recognizing Mori-sumi's skill in {{ill|Kyūjutsu|en|Kyūjutsu|qid=Q11687476|lt=archery}}, persuaded Yoritomo to allow Mori-sumi to demonstrate his abilities before his execution. At the {{ill|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|en|Tsurugaoka Hachimangū|qid=Q701403|lt=Tsurugaoka Hachimangū}} during the {{ill|Life release|en|Life release|qid=Q11078912|lt=Hōjōe}}, Mori-sumi performed an exceptional feat of {{ill|Yabusame|en|Yabusame|qid=Q1886157|lt=yabusame}}, accurately shooting eight targets, their fragments, and the stands holding them. Impressed, Yoritomo pardoned him. Following Kagetoki's further petitions, several of Yoshinaka's retainers were also spared and became {{ill|Gokenin|en|Gokenin|qid=Q63765|lt=gokenin}}.<ref>[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E8%AB%8F%E8%A8%AA%E7%9B%9B%E6%BE%84-1084644 ''Suwa Mori-sumi''] - Kotobank</ref>

In {{ill|Kenkyū|en|Kenkyū|qid=Q1193933|lt=Kenkyū}} 4 (1193), Mori-sumi accompanied Yoritomo on hunts in {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|en|Shimotsuke Province|qid=Q1053699|lt=Shimotsuke Province}} and {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|qid=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province}}, where he continued to serve at ceremonial events involving archery. By 1203, his activities are still noted in historical records. In modern-day {{ill|Shimosuwa|en|Shimosuwa|qid=Q1204211|lt=Shimosuwa}}, a mound called "Kajiwara Zuka" commemorates Mori-sumi's gratitude to Kagetoki.
